headline: RBA Minutes Show Why Three Members Opposed November Rate Rise
deck: The dissenters said earlier tightening needed more time to work through Australia’s economy.
body: The Reserve Bank of Australia’s November minutes show that six of nine board members supported raising the cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85%, while three preferred to leave it at 4.60%. [E2]

The minority said it was prudent to allow more time to assess how the 100 basis points of tightening already delivered would affect the economy; the minutes say they viewed the September tightening as a response to upside inflation risks. [E1][E3]

evidence_box.fragment: These members judged that, having tightened policy in September to mitigate the upside risks to inflation, it was prudent to leave more time to assess how the 100 basis points of tightening already delivered would affect the economy.
